questions.question: A country exporting raw ore and importing finished machinery has the classic peripheral trade profile because:
options: Most value is added in processing, so it is exporting cheap and importing expensive
Machinery cannot be produced in developing countries

questions.question: Commodity dependence is described as living on a rollercoaster because:
options: World-market commodity prices swing violently with global supply and demand that no small producer controls — Zambia rises and falls with copper
Commodities can only be sold once

questions.question: The balance of trade is:
options: The ratio of export prices to import prices
The difference between exports and imports — a surplus when exports exceed imports
The value of goods passing through ports

questions.question: South Africa's encouraging exception among its major exports is:
options: Vehicles built in Gqeberha, East London, Durban and Pretoria — manufactured, value-added exports

subtopics.title: Terms of Trade and Trading Relationships

questions.question: A country's terms of trade deteriorate when:
options: Import prices rise faster than its export prices, so it must export ever more to afford the same imports

questions.question: Primary exporters face long-run deteriorating terms of trade because:
options: Raw materials become heavier over time
Raw materials face competition and substitution while manufactured goods carry technology, branding and patents that protect their prices
Shipping costs only affect raw materials

questions.question: The trading relationship that gives South African vehicles and fruit preferential access to the United States market is:
options: The African Continental Free Trade Area

questions.question: Rich-country farm subsidies are the sore point of protectionism because:
options: They raise food prices in Europe
They apply only to luxury crops
They let European and American produce undercut African farmers in the farmers' own markets

subtopics.title: Globalisation and Its Impact on Development

questions.question: The drivers of globalisation named in the lesson are:
options: Cheaper transport — above all the shipping container — instant communication, and lower trade barriers

questions.question: A transnational corporation (TNC) is:
options: A company operating across many countries — headquarters in one, factories in others, markets everywhere — such as Toyota or MTN

questions.question: The 'race to the bottom' refers to:
options: TNCs using their mobility to demand tax breaks and lax regulation, relocating whenever cheaper labour appears elsewhere
Countries competing to devalue their currencies

questions.question: South Africa's clothing and textile job losses illustrate which cost of globalisation?
options: Local industries being crushed by cheaper imports before they can compete

questions.question: South Korea's export-led recipe ran:
options: Cheap-labour manufactures first, foreign exchange reinvested in education and infrastructure, then climbing the value ladder from textiles to steel to ships to cars to semiconductors
Import substitution behind closed borders throughout
Agriculture only, followed directly by services

questions.question: The comparison that measures the Tigers' achievement is:
options: In 1960 South Korea's income per person resembled Ghana's; within two generations it joined the developed world

questions.question: A structural criticism of export-led development as a universal recipe is:
options: Exports are always less profitable than domestic sales
The strategy requires no state involvement
It needs open, growing world markets — and if every country tries simultaneously, the markets flood

questions.question: Obstacles South Africa faces that the Tigers did not include:
options: No access to any trade agreements
Distance from major markets, electricity insecurity, skills shortages and rigid input costs

questions.question: In the street picture, the spaza selling cheap raw goods while buying expensive processed goods represents:
options: Countries exporting raw materials while importing manufactured goods — money trickling one way

questions.question: The coffee bean earning a few rand raw but hundreds once roasted, branded and served shows:
options: That value added stays where the processing happens, not where the bean grew
That farming is more profitable than retail
That transport is the main cost

questions.question: South Africa 'plays both parts' on the street because:
options: It imports both raw and processed goods
It refuses to trade in raw materials
It sells raw platinum, coal and iron ore like a spaza, but also exports finished vehicles like a supermarket

subtopics.title: Swapping Bags of Oranges for Phones

questions.question: When one phone cost one bag of oranges last year but three bags this year, the orange seller's:
options: Terms of trade have deteriorated — more exports buy the same imports
Balance of trade is in surplus

questions.question: The swap rate drifts against raw sellers because:
options: Anyone can grow oranges but few firms make phones, and the phone-makers hold the patents and brands that protect their prices

questions.question: The African Continental Free Trade Area is a 'team rule' aimed at:
options: Dropping trade fees between neighbours so Africa can trade with Africa instead of only shipping raw goods north

questions.question: Fair trade schemes protect the farmer by:
options: Guaranteeing a floor price plus a social premium, so the swap rate cannot collapse under her

questions.question: The rungs of the Tiger ladder, in order, were:
options: T-shirts, then schools and steel, then ships, then cars, then computer chips

questions.question: 'The ladder needs someone at the top buying' warns that:
options: Export-led growth depends on open, absorbing rich markets, which cannot take every country's exports at once

questions.question: 'The bottom rungs are brutal' refers to:
options: The first generation working long hours for low pay so the next can study engineering — the human cost of early export-led growth
The difficulty of learning to sew

questions.question: South Africa's 'heavy backpack' on the ladder consists of:
options: Load-shedding, distance from major markets and a skills gap — burdens the Tigers did not carry
